title: Fisetin suppresses cigarette smoke extract-induced epithelial to mesenchymal transition of airway epithelial cells through regulating COX-2/MMPs/beta-catenin pathway.
authors: Agraval, Hina; Sharma, Jiten R; Prakash, Nutan; Yadav, Umesh C S
one_liner_zh: 该文研究黄酮类化合物fisetin抑制香烟烟雾提取物诱导的气道上皮细胞上皮间质转化，机制涉及COX-2/MMPs/β-catenin通路，仅含分子对接但无蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Cigarette smoke exposure leads to upregulation of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2), an inducible enzyme that synthesizes prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) and promotes airway inflammation. COX-2 overexpression is frequently implicated in inflammation, invasion, metastasis, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). However, its detailed molecular mechanism in cigarette smoke induced EMT is not clear. Further, fisetin, a bioflavonoid, exhibits antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties, but its effect in modulating COX-2-mediated inflammation and downstream sequelae remains unexplored. Therefore, we have investigated the mechanism of cigarette smoke-induced COX-2-mediated EMT in airway epithelial cells and examined the role of fisetin in controlling this aberration. MTT, trypan blue staining, gelatin zymography, Western blotting, invasion, wound healing, and tumor sphere formation assays in cigarette smoke extract (CSE) and/or fisetin treated airway epithelial cells, and in-silico molecular docking studies were performed. Results revealed that CSE exposure increased the expression and activity of COX-2, MMP-2/9, and beta-catenin and also enhanced expression of EMT markers leading to higher migration and invasion potential of airway epithelial cells. A specific COX-2 inhibitor NS-398 as well as fisetin treatment reversed the expression of EMT biomarkers, reduced the activity of MMP-2/9, and blocked the migration and invasion potential induced by CSE. Further, PGE2 also increased MMPs activity, invasion, and migration potential similar to CSE, which were significantly reversed by fisetin. In-silico studies showed a high binding affinity of fisetin to key EMT associated proteins, validating its anti-EMT potential. Thus, our study firstly unearths the mechanism of CSE-induced EMT in airway epithelial cells via COX-2/MMP/beta-catenin pathway, and secondly, it reveals that fisetin could significantly reverse CSE-induced EMT by inhibiting COX-2, indicating that fisetin could be an effective drug candidate for cigarette smoke-induced lung dysfunction.
abstract_zh: 香烟烟雾暴露导致环氧合酶-2（COX-2）上调，这是一种诱导型酶，可合成前列腺素E2（PGE2）并促进气道炎症。COX-2的过表达常涉及炎症、侵袭、转移及上皮-间质转化（EMT）。然而，其在香烟烟雾诱导的EMT中的详细分子机制尚不清楚。此外，非瑟酮（fisetin）作为一种生物黄酮类化合物，具有抗氧化和抗炎特性，但其在调节COX-2介导的炎症及下游后果中的作用仍未探索。因此，我们研究了香烟烟雾诱导的气道上皮细胞中COX-2介导的EMT机制，并考察了非瑟酮在控制这一异常中的作用。在香烟烟雾提取物（CSE）和/或非瑟酮处理的气道上皮细胞中进行了MTT、台盼蓝染色、明胶酶谱法、Western blotting、侵袭、伤口愈合和肿瘤球形成实验，并进行了计算机分子对接研究。结果显示，CSE暴露增加了COX-2、MMP-2/9和β-catenin的表达及活性，并增强了EMT标志物的表达，导致气道上皮细胞迁移和侵袭能力增强。特异性COX-2抑制剂NS-398以及非瑟酮处理逆转了EMT生物标志物的表达，降低了MMP-2/9的活性，并阻断了CSE诱导的迁移和侵袭能力。此外，PGE2也增加了MMPs活性、侵袭和迁移能力，与CSE类似，这些效应被非瑟酮显著逆转。计算机研究显示，非瑟酮与关键EMT相关蛋白具有高结合亲和力，验证了其抗EMT潜力。因此，我们的研究首先揭示了CSE通过COX-2/MMP/β-catenin通路诱导气道上皮细胞EMT的机制，其次表明非瑟酮可通过抑制COX-2显著逆转CSE诱导的EMT，提示非瑟酮可能成为香烟烟雾诱导的肺功能障碍的有效候选药物。
